app/src/server/format.js:0 / format.js — no JSDoc or types at the API boundary; data shapes are implicit optional-chained object access
churn_resistance.rationale: Good isolation: data access, routing and markup each live in one well-defined module shared by server and client, and no framework internals are relied on. The main churn risk is the hand-rolled HTML string templating, where correctness depends on remembering to escape each interpolation rather than on a safe-by-default primitive.

findings.issue: Server-side fetch has no timeout or abort; a slow or hung API request stalls page rendering forever, and the in-flight promise is cached until it settles.
findings.suggestion: Use fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) }) and surface the failure as a 502/500 instead of hanging the response.

findings.issue: Moves table interpolates API-sourced values (level, power, accuracy, pp) without escapeHtml, unlike every other interpolation in the file; a hostile/changed API payload could inject markup.
findings.suggestion: Escape all cell values (or route them through a small safe-numeric formatter) so the escaping convention is uniform.

findings.issue: `npm run dev` runs the production server in fallback mode serving raw source files, bypassing Vite's dev server and HMR entirely; Vite is effectively only used for `vite build`.
findings.suggestion: Either wire Vite's dev server (middleware mode) behind the custom SSR server, or accept and document that Vite is build-only — right now it's an unexplained half-adoption.

findings.issue: HTML is built by concatenated template strings with manually applied escapeHtml; future edits to pages will need to remember escaping at every new interpolation point.
findings.suggestion: Centralize escaping (e.g. a tagged template literal like html`...` that escapes interpolations by default) so safety is structural rather than conventional.

findings.issue: app/dist/ build output is not gitignored, so build artifacts sit in the repo alongside sources.
findings.suggestion: Add `app/dist/` (or `dist/`) to .gitignore; the manifest is already regenerated by `npm run build`.

findings.issue: Changing the Game select triggers a full page navigation (location.assign) while everything else on the page updates client-side; a mixed interaction model that future feature work may need to unify.
findings.suggestion: Fine as a deliberate trade-off for server-rendered moves tables, but note it so future interactivity doesn't assume SPA-style navigation everywhere.

findings.issue: No JSDoc types on the API-shaped helpers (names entries, species summaries, move rows), so boundary contracts are implicit.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc typedefs for the main API records (or adopt TypeScript) so data-shape changes surface at the boundary.

findings.issue: Legacy `-webkit-text-size-adjust` vendor prefix despite Chromium-only being required.
findings.suggestion: Use the unprefixed `text-size-adjust` (supported in Chromium) or drop it for a Chromium-only target.

summary: A lean, current-generation vanilla setup: zero runtime dependencies, Vite 8 at the exact current stable version used only as a bundler, native fetch/URL/History/CSS-platform features throughout, and server/client markup that can't drift because it's generated from the same shared modules. The main forward-looking weaknesses are the hand-rolled string templating whose escaping convention new code can silently break, and no timeout on server-side API fetches. Overall this code will age well; a safe-by-default template helper and abortable fetches would close the remaining gaps.
